description.value: This study examined whether maternal stimuli modulate amygdala–prefrontal circuitry and affect-related regulatory behavior in children and adolescents.

value: We hypothesized that maternal stimuli might induce phasic modulation of amygdala–mPFC circuitry to promote emotion regulation in childhood by modulating amygdala–mPFC connectivity (instantiating mature-like connectivity) and reducing amygdala and affective reactivity.
We anticipated that this effect would be absent in adolescence

description.value: Participants completed two sessions: behavioral measures and an affect-related regulation task in the first session, followed by the mother/stranger fMRI task in the second session.

spans.text: The task was administered twice, once in the presence of the participant's mother and once in the presence of a stranger (a research assistant).

name.value: Effect of Mother on Amygdala Reactivity

spans.text: ##### Effect of Mother on Amygdala Reactivity

definition.value: A mother/stranger condition x age interaction demonstrated that differential activation to the mother versus stranger stimuli depended on age.

value: Specifically, right amygdala reactivity in children, which is typically high (Gee, Humphreys, et al., 2013), was suppressed when viewing their mother, relative to the stranger condition.
By contrast, adolescents did not show differential amygdala reactivity to mother versus stranger.

spans.text: Specifically, right amygdala reactivity in children, which is typically high ( Gee, Humphreys, et al., 2013 ), was suppressed when viewing their mother, relative to the stranger condition ( Figure 1 ). By contrast, adolescents did not show differential amygdala reactivity to mother versus stranger.
The right amygdala was defined using the Talairach & Tournoux Atlas in AFNI.
